content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass, aiming for a Blizzard-style stocky dwarf with exaggerated proportions, using gradient and mottled paint techniques for a hand-painted look.

Working out the skeleton now: short legs for the 1.3m height, a spine chain built from catmull points running from hips up to the chest, with joint names assigned per segment. I'm planning to loft the torso stations along that spine chain for the skin.

Now I'm sketching rough coordinates: feet at y=0, ankle 0.08, knee 0.28, hip 0.55, shoulders at 0.95 with width ±0.3, head center around 1.12 with an oversized radius near 0.14, helmet topping out near 1.3. Arms branch from the shoulder joint through an elbow offset forward and down toward the wrist.

For the weapon, I'll have the right hand grip the blunderbuss near its wrist, angling the barrel forward and slightly upward at the hip, while the left arm hangs loosely with an open hand rather than forcing a bent port-arms pose.

Working out the gun's grip point, axis direction, and butt placement relative to the hand bone...

Shaping a short flared blunderbuss barrel, lathed from a small base radius out to a brass bell-mouth at the muzzle, with a darker disc suggesting the hollow bore.

Still tracing the outline path...

Adding torus-based barrel bands and a ramrod, shifting the muzzle bell to brass with a gradient blend against the steel barrel. I'll skip heavy engraving but consider a subtle rune decal on the stock's cheek-plate for character.

For the body, I'm planning boots with toe caps and building the legs as chain sweeps from hip to knee to ankle with named joints, giving smooth tapered limbs.

Adding a toe cap sphere, then working out joint naming conventions and setting up torso loft stations with pelvis, waist, chest, and shoulder cross-sections to build a barrel chest with belly shape.

Now I'm defining the spine chain bones from hips up through chest with named joints, then adding the neck and head joints extending from the chest tip upward.

For the head, I'm sketching a skull as an ellipsoid shape with skin-colored material, then starting to place facial features like a bulbous nose sphere positioned forward and slightly down on the face.

Now I'm adding a brow ridge capsule and small deep-set eyes with dark pupils and blue irises, dwarf-style. Then I'm designing a thick braided beard in ginger-orange, built as a tapering capsule mass with two side braids made of small spheres strung along curved paths and finished with brass bead rings.

Still writing beard and mustache geometry...

Now thinking through the helmet design—an iron cap helm with brass rivets, considering a spiked crest or small curved horns to fit the dwarf aesthetic.

Still writing lathe helm coordinates...

Actually I should scale down overall height a bit, lowering the torso and head positions so the total stands closer to 1.3-1.4m. I'm redefining key body heights: hips at 0.56, spine points rising to chest top near 0.95, shoulders at 0.88, neck base around 0.94, and head center at 1.08 with the skull radius adjusted accordingly.

Now I'm working out the helmet dome and spike placement on top of the skull, then setting leg joint positions (hip, knee, ankle) and arm joint positions (shoulder, elbow, wrist) with proportionate lengths, plus sizing the hand spheres slightly oversized for a stylized look.

I'm deciding how to handle fingers for a full skeleton rig — rather than modeling individual digits, I'll add simple thumb and finger joints per hand as rigid capsule parts attached to the wrist bone, keeping the rig manageable while still giving grip detail.

Now I'm computing coordinates for the right arm: setting the wrist position, deriving the hand sphere center from it, and using that as the gun grip point. I'm calculating the gun's forward direction vector and using it to place the stock butt position relative to the grip, checking that the resulting x-coordinate clears the torso.

The muzzle position comes from extending along the same forward direction, giving a total gun length that's a bit oversized for a blunderbuss but acceptable. Now I'm thinking about the left arm pose, considering whether the left hand should support the fore-end of the gun or rest neutrally at the belt, since reaching forward to the gun's position would require an unnatural stretch.

I settle on keeping the left hand relaxed, closed in a fist at the side, with a powder horn hanging from a strap at the hip instead of being held in-hand. For the arm proportions, I'm setting upper arm and forearm radii with brass-trimmed leather bracers, and planning oversized Blizzard-style pauldrons built from partial domed spheres with spikes and rivets for that heroic shoulder silhouette.

Now I'm defining the color palette, going for an Alliance dwarf scheme: blue tunic, steel plate gray, gold trim, brown leather, ruddy skin, and a red-orange beard with warm highlights, plus darker tones for trousers, boots, and metal accents to give depth.

I'm thinking through hand-painted gradient shading for the torso, countershading the cloth light near the chest and dark toward the hem, with a subtle mottle texture overlay for a worn, painted look rather than flat colors. For the tabard, I'll skip any emblem or logo and instead use generic gold stripes or chevron patterns, then add a belt, buckle, and extruded tabard flap slabs.

Now I'm working out the skirt below the belt — a ring of leather pteruges flaps around the hips using a lathe-generated cone shape, with the outline tapering from a narrower radius near the waist to wider at the thigh, built as a thin solid shell for a believable armored skirt.

Adding paint details...

Still working out belt proportions...

Now I'm placing the skirt geometry to properly cover the belt, checking that its depth stays within the leg silhouette at the hips. I'm also planning accessories: a gold buckle at the belt front, pouches on each hip, a powder horn near the gun on the right side, and a diagonal bandolier with shot loops across the chest.

For the bandolier I'm sketching it as a closed loop wrapping both front and back of the torso, running from the right shoulder diagonally across the chest to the left hip, adjusting its depth to sit under the beard without clipping through it.

Computing the diagonal bandolier path...

For the brass cartridges, I need them perpendicular to the strap rather than aligned with it, so instead of using the tangent frame directly I should set orientation via a direction vector to get the cylinder's axis crossing the strap correctly.

I'll place each cartridge at its strap point, slightly lifted so it reads as embedded rather than floating, and trust that the part-level frame placement handles bone weighting automatically along the torso drape.

For the backpack, I'm sketching a leather box pack against the lower back with a rolled bedroll cylinder strapped on top, a hanging tin cup for detail, and shoulder straps swept as curves over to the front — keeping the part count compact given how many elements are accumulating already.

Writing geometry helpers...

Defining more color constants...

I'll build a reusable hand-painted helper combining mottled highlight and shadow colors with countershading, so top-facing surfaces get a painted highlight and undersides get shadow. I'll apply this across armor, cloth, leather, and skin, using a 2048 paint size per part within a 4096 atlas for good detail without excess cost.

For the final palette, I'll keep flat colors under 64 total, sharing paints like skin, beard, steel, gold, blue, leather, wood, and boot tones, with the beard using grained highlight/shadow countershading and metal using mottled scratches over a base steel tone. Now I'm starting the build function definition with the model's name and paint settings.

Setting up skeleton joints...

Continuing to define the neck, head, and jaw joints with their parent links, positions, and aim directions to establish the facial skeletal chain.

Now I'm working out the arm chains for each side, placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints with mirrored x-coordinates and checking that the resulting upper/lower arm bone lengths look proportionate.

Defining sweep radii for the arm tubes...

Rigging the bracer rod to the elbow joint bone explicitly, then building a pauldron as a scaled hemisphere sphere attached to the shoulder joint.

The hemisphere should open downward and tilt outward, which I'll achieve by using a z-axis rotation (mirrored by side) so the dome faces away from the body over the shoulder. I'm also layering a torus brim and additional overlapping lame plates slightly lower and larger for a stacked armor plate look.

Setting the torus axis to "z" with a tilt direction vector so it orients correctly on the dome, then sketching a spike helper for the pauldron using a base-to-tip cone definition...

Now I'm reconsidering rivets on the pauldron rim — decided tilting the domes would make rivets float awkwardly, so I'm dropping the tilt and keeping the pauldrons flat, placing rivets by simple angle positions instead.

For the hands, I'm computing wrist offsets to form a fist position, then deriving the right hand's grip point from the wrist location so the gun can be placed relative to it.

Now I'm figuring out finger placement - I want small capsules wrapping around the stock, with knuckles on the outer side and fingertips curling toward the inner side of the hand.

Adding joints for thumbs and fingers...

Now for legs I'm defining the sweep radii and color bands along each leg path, splitting pants fabric from boot leather at roughly the knee transition point.

Still working out body proportions...

Adding more loft stations...

Then I'm thinking through shoulder width and bone attachment for the torso, making broad dwarf proportions with pauldrons in mind, plus adding a chest plate or gorget layered over the tunic.

Defining the collar outline...

Then I'll add a neck cylinder connecting the gorget to the head, and consider gold trim stripes on the tunic as a decorative placket.

Now I'm working through torso paint logic for a center gold stripe and bottom hem trim, plus a pack rig on the back. For the head, I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere on the head bone, then adding a separate jaw piece as another scaled sphere.

Adding cheek, nose, and brow details...

Working out ear scaling with gold earring rings, then skipping extra details like cheek rosiness and scars. For the beard and mustache, I'm defining a lofted path going down from the chin with width/height stations tapering toward the bottom, planning a catmull-rom curve for smooth downward flow.

For the beard's orientation, the normal faces forward with depth and width mapped to the loft, rigging it to the head bone, and tapering the tip to a small rounded cap. I'm narrowing the main beard mass and adding separate side braids hanging from the cheeks down past the jaw to keep them visually distinct from the central beard volume.

Rethinking the design, I decide to braid the central beard into one large hero braid splitting into two long strands that hang down over the chest to about y 0.58-0.62, finished with gold clasps and tassels for a more recognizable silhouette. I'm defining the loft stations for this upper beard mass, tapering width and depth as it descends from y 1.04 down toward y 0.8.

Writing braid sweep code...

Adding the tip bands with a gold clasp cylinder and ring, plus a tassel spike tail trailing below the braid, checking the braid stays visibly separated from the torso. I'm also working out the mustache sweep with thinned tips and a handlebar curl, then starting the sideburn hair strands that curve from the ears into the beard using catmull splines.

For texture, I'm scattering strand cards across the beard surface using an orange leaf-shaped SVG texture with a darker center line, tuning card size, lean, and bend so the default flow direction naturally droops downward against the beard's front-facing normal. I'm leaving eyebrows uncarded for now but planning similar card strands for a red horsehair helm crest.

Now I'm designing the crest shape itself as an extruded outline near the top of the helm — a non-self-crossing polygon running from back to front with a curved peak, smoothed and colored red with a gold stripe, positioned so its base merges cleanly into the dome.

Next I'm working out the dome and helm geometry: setting precise heights for the dome profile and crest base so they fit inside each other, then lathing the helm shape with a stepped outline from base to peak, flat steel shading. I'm adding a gold brim band as a torus at the helm's base and placing eight rivets evenly around it.

For the nose guard, I'm sketching a tapered steel rod running from the top of the helm down toward the nose but stopping short so it clears the nose tip, accounting for the helm sitting above the eyebrows. I'm also starting to plan curved bezier-swept cheek horns extending outward and upward from the sides of the helm, ram-horn style.

Writing horn sweep geometry...

Now I'm moving on to gun details, figuring out how to reference the right wrist joint from the arm chain for attaching the weapon.

Building the gun geometry now...

Positioning the decal plane on the stock's outer face, adjusting for width tapering and facing it outward with a gold filigree texture. Then moving to the barrel, planning a lathe-generated bell shape along the main axis, keeping total gun length consistent with the butt position.

I'm shortening the barrel to about 0.5m with a tapered outline profile and ten lathe segments, since full length would overshoot a realistic blunderbuss size. For paint, I'm applying a gradient between dark steel and gold at specific points along the barrel, then adding a dark bore cylinder near the muzzle end.

Now I'm closing off the bore floor with a dark disc and considering gold tori as decorative barrel bands at two points along the length, then moving on to roughing out the lock plate as a small steel box mounted on the barrel's side.

Next I'm sketching the hammer mechanism as a curved steel rod sweeping up to a cocked spike shape with a small flash pan above it, then building the trigger guard as a gold curved sweep beneath the grip with a small rod for the trigger itself, before starting the wooden fore-end under the barrel.

I'm layering a countershaded wood grain texture running along the stock, then sketching a powder horn as a curved sweep hanging near the left hip, positioning it against where the arm hangs down.

I'll attach the horn near the hip joint with a gold cap at the base and a strap sweeping down to the belt, then add a leather pouch at the front-left hip, checking its position against the skirt's elliptical boundary so it sits naturally on top.

Next I'm placing the backpack against the torso's back curve, sizing it to roughly 0.34x0.34x0.16 with enough gap to avoid clipping, and adding a cylindrical bedroll attached to it.

Then I'm figuring out the bedroll's rotation and position so it sits above the pack without colliding with the head, plus adding two leather strap tori around it, a small flap box with gold buckles for the pack lid, and considering a hanging pot detail.

I'm adding a tin cup with a loop handle beside the pack and sketching shoulder strap curves running from the pack top over the shoulder to the chest and down to the waist, though the geometry is getting fiddly so I may simplify or skip the front straps.

Rather than hand-fitting exact torso dimensions at each point, I decide to use a drape function that pulls rough strap points onto the nearest body surface, checking that the back-bottom point lands reasonably on the torso's back curve.

I'm extracting the torso, hips, and beard surfaces for draping and skinning purposes. I'll skip extra accessories like a cloak, hand-axe, or spyglass trinket to keep the part count reasonable, and the character will just stand on the ground without a separate base.

Now I'm checking the mouth cavity placement under the mustache, then verifying the beard doesn't clip through the skull's front surface near the jaw. I'm also checking the right arm's gun placement against the forearm and wrist geometry to make sure the stock and barrel don't overlap the arm tube awkwardly.

Design is finalized — now moving to writing the actual TypeScript code, starting with the imports for Three.js and the builder utility.

I'll use glow sparingly for the iris and a ruby gem set into the gun stock, and set up the metadata export with name, description, and style info. Then I'm writing a `hand` paint helper that combines mottled highlight and lowlight tones with countershading for a skin-like texture.

For the tunic, I'm defining a paint function that assigns gold or blue based on vertical position and a thin centerline stripe, accounting for the collar and skirt covering certain areas. I'm setting up leg and boot colors using the hand helper with brown and dark leather tones, then starting an SVG texture for gold filigree trim using a wavy path pattern.

For the strand texture, I'm shaping a teardrop-like path with a pointed tip at the top and rounded root at the bottom, matching the card's coordinate system, plus an inner highlight stroke and a second darker variant for contrast.

Now I'm setting up the card scattering across the beard with scale and lean/bend variance, plus a separate point scatter with a minimum distance and a normal-based filter to avoid placing hits on the underside. Then I'm starting the actual build function, initializing the builder and random seed to begin constructing the dwarf rifleman model.

Setting up part placement helper...

Defining sweep radius bands...

Placing the hand sphere at the wrist joint with a slight scale adjustment for a natural shape, then adding a finger joint positioned and aimed relative to the hand for proper digit orientation.

Now I'm positioning the thumb slightly inward toward the body with its own aim target, then building capsule shapes for the four fingers, spacing them along the hand's front edge to simulate a gripping pose around the stock.

Placing fingers wrapped underneath the stock with the thumb resting on top, using skin-colored capsules for the digits, then adding a bracer rod along the forearm to represent the gauntlet.

I'm attaching the bracer to the elbow joint with tapered radii and flat caps, considering a short gold band accent, then move to finalizing the legs with contact options and placing a small glowing octahedron gem on the stock's side.

Checking type signatures for parts and joints, confirming the bezier curve helper takes four control points, and setting direction vectors for part placement. For the lathe geometry, I'm working out how to type the outline points correctly—defining a helper to coerce coordinate arrays into the proper tuple format so I can pass literals inline without mismatches.

I'm adding a tabard flap using extrude with a front-facing outline, giving it thickness and coloring it blue with gold trim by painting stripes based on surface coordinates, avoiding the lathe smoothing option since it tends to throw errors, and using underscore-prefixed unused parameters in the paint callbacks.

Now I'm working out the geometry so the tabard follows the skirt's outward slope -- checking the skirt radius at different heights and angling the tabard's local y-axis slightly forward so it tracks the flare rather than floating away from the body.

I still need a hip bone, and there's a leftover back skirt tail I'll skip for now. I'm also handling the remaining foot details -- toe, heel, ankle placement where the leg tube meets the ground, and the radius array for the leg's chain sweep with its two spans.

Now I'm putting together the torus pieces for the ears and earring, then writing out the complete file.
